THIS APPEAL IS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
 THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:21032  MFA No. 4689 of 2020  JUDGMENT

This appeal by the Insurance Company is filed under Section 173(1) of the Indian Motor Vehicles Act, challenging the judgment and award dated January 21, 2020, passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru, in MVC No. 4387/2018.

2. The respondent, having sustained injuries in a road traffic accident on April 26, 2018, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Indian Motor Vehicles Act seeking just and proper compensation.
The tribunal, after attributing 10% contributory negligence to the claimant, awarded a total compensation of Rs.4,80,770/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum.

3. Upon hearing the learned counsel for both the appellant and the respondent, the following points were considered:
i) The accident occurred in 2018.
In the absence of proof of income, the claimant's notional income was assessed at Rs.12,500/- per month, as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka Legal Aid Services Authority.
The doctor assessed the disability to the claimant's lower limb at 37%.
However, the tribunal assessed the functional disability at 10% instead of the 14% that might have been more appropriate.
ii) The evidence provided by RW.1, the Investigating Officer, and the spot sketch indicated that the claimant was also negligent.
Given the evidence on record, it is appropriate to NC: 2024:KHC:21032 attribute 20% contributory negligence to the claimant, instead of the 10% attributed by the tribunal.
iii) The tribunal assessed the claimant's income at Rs.9,000/- per month, which is lower than the notional income of Rs.12,500/- per month.
Additionally, the compensation awarded under other heads was also on the lower side.

4. Considering these factors, it is determined that the compensation amount of Rs.4,32,693/-
awarded by the tribunal is just and proper.
However, the interest rate of 9% per annum awarded by the tribunal is on the higher side.
